td_status: Visual estimate; no metric geometry or UV measurement.

prompts.side: Re-render the fictional 3D game asset in image 1. Preserve its geometry, framing, silhouette, part proportions, wood and blued steel colors, and strict side orthographic, butt left, muzzle right camera. Change only the apparent texel density of its surface albedo. Image 2 is solely a texel-size and shading sample from another game asset; never depict that sample subject or its colors. Aim visually for 30 texture pixels per meter: replace the previous fine texture with clearly much larger, sparse square texels, sampled nearest-neighbor, with adjacent texels forming simple restrained clusters. As a visual calibration, use roughly thirty-odd texel columns along the long object and only a handful across the stock height; in front view, just a few texels across each material zone. This is not an image-wide pixel effect: texture squares wrap and foreshorten on the 3D surfaces; the silhouette, bevels and studio illumination remain clean and smooth, exactly as on a low-poly game model. Walnut becomes a few broad warm patches with a very restrained suggestion of grain. Steel has large subtle blue-gray blocks with no scratches, fine speckles, tiny marks or noisy checkerboard. Keep the full prop on the same warm off-white background, no labels or other objects.
